page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz and includes 8 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the t3a.xlarge sits primarily in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show weak performance, with read-only large block speeds at 23.87 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.7 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in the PassMark CPU encryption test, scoring 3207.35. Other workloads, such as static web serving at 2.73 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 2.53 million operations per second, fall into the bottom 10%.

The t3a.xlarge utilizes a burstable CPU allocation model, which offers a cost-effective solution for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that experience occasional spikes. This resource-density profile makes it qualitatively efficient for budget-conscious deployments, provided the CPU credit balance is managed. The primary tradeoff is the low sustained compute and memory performance, as shown by the poor benchmark results in compilation, image processing, and text processing.

This instance is suited for low-traffic web servers, small development environments, code repositories, and light background tasks. It is not recommended for compute-intensive applications, large databases, or high-throughput data processing due to its burstable CPU limits and lower benchmark scores.
